title: Obstetric critical care
summary: Obstetric critical care: severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia, postpartum haemorrhage (WHO 2025 MOTIVE bundle), HELLP and AFLP, maternal sepsis, peripartum cardiomyopathy, and maternal cardiac arrest with amniotic fluid embolism.

topics.title: Severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia
topics.summary: Treat BP ≥ 160/110 within 30-60 min, give magnesium sulfate (Pritchard or Zuspan), restrict fluids, manage seizures and plan delivery.

definition.text: Pre-eclampsia: new hypertension (≥ 140/90) after 20 weeks with proteinuria or maternal organ dysfunction (renal, liver, neurological, haematological) or uteroplacental dysfunction. Severe features include BP ≥ 160/110, platelets < 100,000, liver enzymes > 2× normal, creatinine > 1.1 mg/dL, pulmonary oedema, headache/visual symptoms. Eclampsia: new-onset seizures.

steps.title: Eclamptic seizure
steps.detail: Left lateral position, airway, oxygen; magnesium 4 g IV over 15-20 min (do not use diazepam first-line). Recurrent seizure: further 2 g IV.

steps.title: Treat severe hypertension
steps.detail: BP ≥ 160/110 confirmed over 15 min: labetalol IV, hydralazine IV or oral immediate-release nifedipine within 30-60 min; target 135/85 (NICE) and < 160/110.

steps.title: Magnesium prophylaxis
steps.detail: All severe pre-eclampsia (during labour/delivery and 24 h after): Pritchard or Zuspan regimen; monitor reflexes, RR, urine output; check levels if oliguric.

steps.title: Fluid restriction
steps.detail: Total fluids about 80 mL/h unless ongoing losses (risk of pulmonary oedema); strict input-output.

steps.title: Investigations
steps.detail: FBC, LFT, LDH, creatinine, uric acid, coagulation, urine protein:creatinine ratio; CT/MRI brain if focal signs, seizures after 48 h postpartum or atypical (PRES, stroke, CVT).

steps.title: Deliver
steps.detail: Delivery is definitive; after stabilisation (≥ 34 weeks or maternal compromise at any gestation); steroids for fetal lung maturity if < 34 weeks and time allows.

steps.title: Postpartum
steps.detail: Continue BP monitoring; risk of eclampsia and stroke persists for days; switch to oral agents (nifedipine/amlodipine, labetalol, enalapril postpartum).

doseCards.dose: 4 g over 15-20 min, then 1 g/h for 24 h
doseCards.dilution: Load: 8 mL of 50% + 12 mL NS (20 mL of 20%); maintenance 25 g (50 mL of 50%) in 500 mL = 50 mg/mL

doseCards.workedExample: 20 mg = 4 mL of 5 mg/mL over 2 min

redFlags.text: Loss of patellar reflexes, RR < 12/min or oliguria on magnesium: stop infusion, check level, give calcium gluconate if respiratory depression.
Severe headache, visual disturbance, epigastric pain or SpO2 falling: imminent eclampsia, HELLP or pulmonary oedema.

pitfalls.text: Liberal IV fluids causing pulmonary oedema (capillary leak, low oncotic pressure).
Using diazepam or phenytoin instead of magnesium for eclampsia.

pearls.text: Magnesium halves the risk of eclampsia (Magpie) and is the anticonvulsant of choice even in seizures after delivery.

nodes.text: Left lateral, airway, MgSO4 4 g IV
Stop Mg, calcium gluconate 1 g, check level
Stabilise and plan delivery; monitor 24-72 h postpartum

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Abnormal placentation with impaired spiral artery remodelling causes placental ischaemia and release of anti-angiogenic factors (sFlt-1, soluble endoglin), producing systemic endothelial dysfunction, vasoconstriction, capillary leak, glomerular endotheliosis and cerebral autoregulatory failure (PRES).
consultantNotes.evidence:
- Magpie (10,141 women): magnesium halved eclampsia risk (RR 0.42) [Magpie 2002].
- ACOG 2020 and ISSHP 2021 guidance on BP thresholds, agents and timing of delivery [ACOG 2020; Magee 2022].
- NICE NG133 BP target 135/85 and fluid restriction [NICE 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies: - 12 vs 24 h postpartum magnesium; Pritchard vs Zuspan; sFlt-1/PlGF testing.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Hypertensive disorders are a leading direct cause of maternal death in India. The Pritchard (IM) regimen is widely used because infusion pumps may be unavailable; MoHFW and FOGSI recommend loading dose before referral from peripheral centres.
- Late presentation with eclampsia and PRES is common in rural India.

topics.title: Postpartum haemorrhage
topics.summary: Early detection (≥ 300-500 mL), the MOTIVE bundle with tranexamic acid, second-line uterotonics, balloon tamponade, surgery and massive transfusion.

definition.text: PPH (WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025): blood loss ≥ 500 mL within 24 h of birth, or ≥ 300 mL with abnormal vital signs. Causes - 4 Ts: Tone (atony, ~70%), Trauma, Tissue (retained placenta), Thrombin (coagulopathy).

steps.title: Detect early
steps.detail: Measure blood loss objectively (calibrated drape, weighing); monitor vital signs and shock index (> 0.9-1 concerning).

steps.title: MOTIVE bundle immediately
steps.detail: Massage of the uterus; Oxytocic (oxytocin 10 units IV/IM + infusion); Tranexamic acid 1 g IV; IV fluids (warmed crystalloid, blood); Vaginal and genital tract examination (tears, retained tissue); Escalation.

steps.title: Second-line uterotonics
steps.detail: Carboprost 250 mcg IM every 15 min (not in asthma), methylergometrine 0.2 mg IM (not in hypertension), misoprostol 800 mcg SL.

steps.title: Call for help and blood
steps.detail: Activate obstetric haemorrhage/massive transfusion protocol; group-specific/O-negative blood; FFP, platelets; keep fibrinogen > 200 mg/dL (cryoprecipitate/fibrinogen concentrate) - fibrinogen < 200 predicts severe PPH.

steps.title: Mechanical and surgical
steps.detail: Bimanual compression, uterine balloon tamponade (Bakri or condom catheter), non-pneumatic anti-shock garment during transfer; laparotomy with compression sutures (B-Lynch), uterine/internal iliac artery ligation, interventional radiology embolisation, hysterectomy.

steps.title: Correct the lethal triad
steps.detail: Warm fluids and patient, ionised Ca > 1.1 mmol/L, avoid acidosis; viscoelastic testing where available.

steps.title: After PPH
steps.detail: HDU/ICU monitoring for re-bleeding, DIC, AKI, Sheehan's; IV iron for anaemia; VTE prophylaxis once bleeding controlled.

doseCards.dose: 10 units slow IV/IM, then 40 units in 500 mL at 125 mL/h
1 g over 10 min; repeat 1 g after 30 min if bleeding continues
doseCards.workedExample: 1 g (10 mL of 100 mg/mL) in 100 mL NS over 10 min

redFlags.text: Shock index > 1 or blood loss > 1,500 mL: major obstetric haemorrhage - activate MTP, senior obstetrician and anaesthetist.

pitfalls.text: Visual estimation underestimates blood loss; young women compensate until late.
Giving TXA after 3 h from birth: benefit falls with delay (most effective early).

pearls.text: Concealed bleeding (broad ligament haematoma, uterine rupture, abruption) - look with ultrasound if shock is out of proportion to visible loss.

nodes.text: Blood loss ≥ 300 mL with abnormal vitals or ≥ 500 mL
MOTIVE: massage, oxytocin, TXA 1 g, IV fluids, examine

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: At term, uterine blood flow is ~700 mL/min; haemostasis depends on myometrial contraction compressing spiral arteries. Atony, trauma or coagulopathy (abruption, AFE, sepsis, dilution) cause rapid haemorrhage; hypofibrinogenaemia develops early.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- WOMAN (20,060 women): TXA reduced death from bleeding (1.5% vs 1.9%), especially within 3 h [WOMAN 2017].
- E-MOTIVE: calibrated drape detection plus bundle reduced severe PPH, laparotomy or death (1.6% vs 4.3%) [Gallos 2023].
- WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025 consolidated PPH guidelines [WHO 2025].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Prophylactic TXA at caesarean; fibrinogen concentrate vs cryoprecipitate; REBOA.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- PPH is the leading cause of maternal death in India; anaemia in pregnancy reduces tolerance to blood loss.
- Condom-catheter balloon tamponade is a low-cost option; carbetocin (heat-stable) and misoprostol are useful where cold chain is unreliable.
- MoHFW programmes (LaQshya, SUMAN) promote PPH drills and blood availability at first referral units.

topics.title: HELLP syndrome and acute fatty liver of pregnancy
topics.summary: Distinguish HELLP from AFLP (Swansea), deliver, support coagulation and glucose, and watch for hepatic haematoma and acute liver failure.

definition.text: HELLP: Haemolysis (LDH > 600 U/L, schistocytes), Elevated Liver enzymes (AST/ALT > 2× normal, ~> 70 U/L), Low Platelets (< 100,000/mm³), usually with pre-eclampsia. AFLP: third-trimester microvesicular fatty liver with hypoglycaemia, coagulopathy, encephalopathy and AKI; diagnosed by Swansea criteria (≥ 6 of 14).

steps.title: Stabilise and treat as severe pre-eclampsia
steps.detail: BP control and magnesium sulfate for HELLP.

steps.title: Work-up
steps.detail: FBC with smear, LDH, bilirubin, AST/ALT, glucose, coagulation including fibrinogen, ammonia, creatinine, uric acid; ultrasound liver (haematoma).

steps.title: Deliver
steps.detail: Both HELLP (≥ 34 weeks or deteriorating) and AFLP require prompt delivery after maternal stabilisation.

steps.title: Correct coagulation
steps.detail: Platelets > 50,000 before caesarean (transfuse if lower); FFP/cryoprecipitate for AFLP coagulopathy guided by fibrinogen and bleeding.

steps.title: Glucose
steps.detail: AFLP: hourly glucose; dextrose infusion (10-20%) for hypoglycaemia.

steps.title: Liver failure care
steps.detail: Encephalopathy, rising INR, lactate: manage as acute liver failure, contact transplant centre; plasma exchange in selected cases.

steps.title: Watch for haematoma
steps.detail: Right upper quadrant/shoulder pain with shock: subcapsular liver haematoma/rupture - CT, interventional radiology or surgery.

tables.title: Swansea criteria for AFLP (≥ 6 without other cause)
rows: Ascites or bright liver on ultrasound
Ammonia > 47 µmol/L; creatinine > 1.7 mg/dL (150 µmol/L); PT > 14 s or aPTT > 34 s
tables.caption: 14 criteria in total.

redFlags.text: Sudden shoulder-tip pain and hypotension in HELLP: liver haematoma rupture - surgical emergency.

pitfalls.text: Missing hypoglycaemia in AFLP presenting as drowsiness.
Labelling AFLP as viral hepatitis and delaying delivery.

pearls.text: In India, also exclude hepatitis E (very high mortality in pregnancy) and malaria/dengue when liver enzymes and platelets are abnormal.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: HELLP is a severe form of pre-eclampsia with microangiopathic haemolysis and periportal hepatic necrosis. AFLP is linked to fetal fatty-acid oxidation defects (LCHAD deficiency), with toxic fetal metabolites causing maternal microvesicular steatosis and mitochondrial dysfunction.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ACOG 2020 defines HELLP and management within pre-eclampsia [ACOG 2020].
- Swansea criteria (prospective Welsh study) for AFLP diagnosis [Ch'ng 2002].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Corticosteroids to raise platelets in HELLP (not shown to improve maternal outcomes); plasma exchange in AFLP.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Acute viral hepatitis E is a major cause of liver failure in pregnancy in India and must be distinguished from AFLP and HELLP.
- Test newborns of AFLP mothers for LCHAD deficiency where available.

topics.title: Sepsis in pregnancy and the puerperium
topics.summary: Recognise sepsis despite physiological changes, give antibiotics within 1 h, find and control the source, and protect both patients.

definition.text: Maternal sepsis: organ dysfunction from infection during pregnancy, childbirth, post-abortion or postpartum period (up to 42 days). Common sources: genital tract (chorioamnionitis, endometritis, septic abortion), urinary tract, pneumonia, wound/breast infection; in India also malaria, dengue, leptospirosis.

steps.title: Recognise
steps.detail: Use an obstetric early warning score; normal pregnancy raises HR and lowers BP and PaCO2, so persistent HR > 110, RR > 24, temperature > 38 °C or < 36 °C, lactate > 2 mmol/L and altered mentation are concerning. Do not use qSOFA alone.

steps.title: Antibiotics within 1 h
steps.detail: Blood cultures, then broad-spectrum: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h (or meropenem if ESBL risk); add clindamycin 900 mg q8h for suspected group A streptococcal or toxic shock; add azithromycin/doxycycline per source (doxycycline after delivery).

steps.title: Resuscitate
steps.detail: Left uterine displacement (> 20 weeks); 1-2 L crystalloid in boluses with reassessment (pulmonary oedema risk); noradrenaline for MAP ≥ 65 mmHg.

steps.title: Source control
steps.detail: Evacuation of retained products, delivery for chorioamnionitis, drainage of abscess, hysterectomy for necrotising myometritis.

steps.title: Fetal considerations
steps.detail: Fetal monitoring when viable; maternal stabilisation is the best fetal resuscitation; delivery is not indicated for maternal sepsis alone unless intrauterine source.

steps.title: Other
steps.detail: VTE prophylaxis, glucose control, steroids for fetal lung maturity if preterm delivery likely; avoid ACE inhibitors and tetracyclines before delivery.

redFlags.text: Severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, rash and shock postpartum: group A streptococcal sepsis - very rapid progression; clindamycin plus beta-lactam and surgical review.

pitfalls.text: Attributing tachycardia and low BP to normal pregnancy.
Supine positioning causing aortocaval compression and worsening hypotension.

pearls.text: Lactate is not increased by normal pregnancy, but can rise during labour.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Pregnancy alters immunity (reduced cell-mediated immunity), raises cardiac output and plasma volume, and lowers colloid osmotic pressure - increasing susceptibility to pulmonary oedema and making shock recognition harder.
consultantNotes.evidence: - SMFM Consult #47 (2019): recognition, antibiotics within 1 h, fluid and vasopressor strategy in pregnancy [Plante 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Best obstetric sepsis screening tool; fluid volume in pregnancy.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Unsafe abortion, home deliveries and prolonged labour contribute to maternal sepsis in India; also consider malaria (severe in pregnancy), dengue, scrub typhus and leptospirosis (doxycycline/azithromycin per stage).
- Hepatitis E causes high mortality in pregnancy.

topics.title: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
topics.summary: Diagnose PPCM by echo, treat heart failure with pregnancy-safe drugs, consider bromocriptine with anticoagulation, and escalate early to mechanical support in shock.

definition.text: PPCM: heart failure with LVEF < 45% towards the end of pregnancy or in the months following delivery (mostly in the first month), with no other identifiable cause.

steps.title: Suspect and confirm
steps.detail: Breathlessness, orthopnoea, oedema late pregnancy/postpartum: BNP/NT-proBNP, ECG, echocardiography; exclude pre-eclampsia, PE, AFE, myocarditis, pre-existing cardiomyopathy.

steps.title: Acute HF
steps.detail: Oxygen/NIV, IV furosemide, nitrates if BP allows; avoid ACEi/ARB/ARNI/MRA/SGLT2i before delivery (use hydralazine-nitrate); beta-blocker (metoprolol) once stable.

steps.title: Cardiogenic shock
steps.detail: Early transfer to a centre with MCS; levosimendan preferred inotrope (catecholamines, especially dobutamine, may be harmful in PPCM); IABP/Impella/VA-ECMO; urgent delivery if antepartum.

steps.title: Bromocriptine
steps.detail: 2.5 mg BD for 2 weeks then daily for 6 weeks (severe, EF < 25% or shock), always with anticoagulation; stops breastfeeding.

steps.title: Anticoagulation
steps.detail: Therapeutic anticoagulation for LV thrombus, AF or EF < 30-35% (high thrombosis risk peripartum); at least prophylactic with bromocriptine.

steps.title: Postpartum
steps.detail: Full guideline-directed HF therapy (ACEi/ARNI, MRA, beta-blocker, SGLT2i if not breastfeeding); counsel on future pregnancy risk.

doseCards.dose: 2.5 mg BD × 2 weeks, then 2.5 mg daily × 6 weeks

redFlags.text: PPCM with hypotension, lactate rise or LVEF < 25%: high risk - transfer early for mechanical circulatory support.

pitfalls.text: Missing PPCM as 'postpartum anaemia' or 'chest infection'.

pearls.text: Enalapril and captopril are compatible with breastfeeding; ARNI and SGLT2 inhibitors are not recommended while breastfeeding.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Oxidative stress cleaves prolactin into a 16-kDa fragment that is anti-angiogenic and cardiotoxic; together with sFlt-1 (high in pre-eclampsia) and genetic predisposition (titin variants), this causes cardiomyocyte and endothelial injury - the rationale for bromocriptine.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- HFA ESC 2019 position statement [Bauersachs 2019]; ESC 2018 pregnancy guidelines [Regitz-Zagrosek 2018].
- Bromocriptine RCT (63 patients): no difference between 1 and 8 weeks; high recovery rates in both [Hilfiker-Kleiner 2017].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Bromocriptine efficacy (no placebo-controlled RCT completed); levosimendan vs other inotropes.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- PPCM incidence is relatively high in parts of India; anaemia, multiparity, pre-eclampsia and malnutrition are associated.
- Mechanical circulatory support is concentrated in metropolitan centres; early referral is crucial.

topics.title: Maternal cardiac arrest and amniotic fluid embolism
topics.summary: High-quality CPR with left uterine displacement, early airway, resuscitative hysterotomy by 5 minutes, and the reversible causes specific to pregnancy.

definition.text: Maternal arrest needs two patients' teams (obstetric, anaesthetic, neonatal). After about 20 weeks (fundus at or above umbilicus) the gravid uterus compresses the aorta and IVC; delivery improves maternal resuscitation.

steps.title: Start CPR and call
steps.detail: Call obstetric arrest team and neonatology; CPR with standard hand position; defibrillate with standard energies (remove fetal monitors).

steps.title: Manual left uterine displacement
steps.detail: Continuous manual displacement to the left (or 15-30° left tilt if on firm surface) when fundus is at or above the umbilicus.

steps.title: Airway and access
steps.detail: Early airway by experienced operator (difficult airway, aspiration risk; smaller tube); IV/IO access above the diaphragm.

steps.title: Resuscitative hysterotomy
steps.detail: If no ROSC by 4 minutes, perform perimortem caesarean delivery at the site of arrest, aiming delivery within 5 minutes of arrest.

steps.title: Reversible causes (BEAU-CHOPS)
steps.detail: Bleeding/DIC, Embolism (PE, AFE), Anaesthetic complications (high block, LAST - lipid), Uterine atony, Cardiac disease (PPCM, MI, dissection), Hypertension/eclampsia/stroke, Others (Hs and Ts), Placenta, Sepsis. Magnesium toxicity: calcium gluconate.

steps.title: Amniotic fluid embolism
steps.detail: Sudden hypoxia, hypotension/arrest and DIC during labour or shortly after: high-quality CPR, early delivery, aggressive correction of coagulopathy (MTP, fibrinogen), RV support (avoid fluid overload, inhaled vasodilators, noradrenaline/dobutamine/milrinone), ECMO where available.

steps.title: Post-arrest
steps.detail: ICU; targeted temperature control avoiding fever; treat cause; neonatal resuscitation team.

redFlags.text: Collapse with hypoxia and bleeding/DIC during or just after delivery: amniotic fluid embolism.

pitfalls.text: Waiting to transfer to theatre for perimortem caesarean: perform it where the arrest occurs.
Stopping CPR to tilt the patient: use manual uterine displacement instead.

pearls.text: Keep a perimortem caesarean kit (scalpel) on every labour ward and emergency resuscitation trolley.

nodes.text: Pregnant patient unresponsive, not breathing normally
CPR, call obstetric/neonatal team, defibrillate if shockable
Manual left uterine displacement; airway; IV above diaphragm

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Aortocaval compression reduces venous return and cardiac output during CPR by up to 30-40%; emptying the uterus restores venous return. Pregnancy increases oxygen consumption and reduces FRC, so hypoxia develops rapidly.
consultantNotes.evidence: - ERC 2025 Special Circumstances [Lott 2025]; AHA 2015 scientific statement [Jeejeebhoy 2015]; SMFM AFE management [Pacheco 2020].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Exact timing of hysterotomy; ECPR in maternal arrest.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Most maternal arrests in India occur in labour rooms of district hospitals; regular drills, a hysterotomy kit and immediate access to blood are key quality measures (LaQshya).

drugs.name: Magnesium sulfate
drugs.indications: Eclampsia treatment; seizure prophylaxis in severe pre-eclampsia
drugs.adultDose: Zuspan (IV): 4 g IV over 15-20 min, then 1 g/h for 24 h. Pritchard (IM, widely used in India): 4 g IV (20%) over 15-20 min + 10 g IM (5 g of 50% in each buttock), then 5 g IM every 4 h in alternate buttocks for 24 h. Recurrent seizure: further 2 g IV.
drugs.preparationIndia: 50% = 0.5 g/mL (1 g in 2 mL); dilute 4 g in NS to 20 mL (20%) for IV loading.
drugs.renalHepatic: Oliguria/raised creatinine: reduce or withhold maintenance and check levels.
drugs.cautions: Toxicity: loss of patellar reflexes (~7-10 mEq/L), respiratory depression, cardiac arrest. Antidote: calcium gluconate 1 g IV.
drugs.monitoring: Before each dose: patellar reflex present, RR > 16/min, urine output > 100 mL/4 h.

drugs.name: Labetalol
drugs.adultDose: 20 mg IV over 2 min; if needed 40 mg after 10 min, then 80 mg every 10 min (max cumulative 300 mg); or infusion 1-2 mg/min.

drugs.name: Hydralazine
drugs.adultDose: 5-10 mg IV over 2 min; repeat 10 mg after 20 min if BP still ≥ 160/110 (max 20 mg bolus doses; then switch agent).
drugs.cautions: Maternal hypotension (give with 250-500 mL crystalloid if dry), tachycardia, headache.
drugs.verify: IV hydralazine availability in India is intermittent.

drugs.name: Nifedipine (immediate-release oral)
drugs.indications: Acute severe hypertension in pregnancy (no IV access)
drugs.adultDose: 10 mg orally; if needed 20 mg after 20 min, then 20 mg after another 20 min; then switch agent.
drugs.cautions: Do not give sublingually; caution with magnesium (theoretical hypotension).

drugs.name: Calcium gluconate 10%
drugs.indications: Magnesium toxicity; hypocalcaemia with massive transfusion
drugs.adultDose: 1 g (10 mL of 10%) IV over 10 min.

drugs.name: Oxytocin
drugs.adultDose: Treatment: 10 units IV slowly (or IM), then infusion 40 units in 500 mL crystalloid at 125 mL/h (10 units/h).
drugs.cautions: Rapid IV bolus causes hypotension; water intoxication with prolonged high doses.

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid
drugs.adultDose: 1 g IV over 10 min as soon as PPH is diagnosed and within 3 h of birth; second 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 min or restarts within 24 h.
drugs.renalHepatic: Reduce repeated doses in severe AKI.

drugs.name: Carboprost (15-methyl PGF2α)
drugs.adultDose: 250 mcg IM (or intramyometrial) every 15 min, max 8 doses (2 mg).

drugs.name: Methylergometrine (ergometrine)
drugs.adultDose: Methylergometrine 0.2 mg IM, may repeat after 15 min (ergometrine 0.5 mg IM per RCOG).

drugs.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
drugs.adultDose: 4.5 g IV q6h (± clindamycin for toxin suppression if GAS/toxic shock suspected).

drugs.name: Clindamycin
drugs.indications: Toxin suppression in group A streptococcal/staphylococcal toxic shock
drugs.adultDose: 900 mg IV q8h with a beta-lactam.

drugs.name: Bromocriptine
drugs.adultDose: 2.5 mg orally twice daily for 2 weeks, then 2.5 mg daily for 6 weeks (severe LVEF < 25%/shock); 2.5 mg daily for 1 week in uncomplicated cases.
drugs.cautions: Thrombosis risk: give with at least prophylactic anticoagulation; stops lactation.
